```{r}
#| label: setup

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)


```

# Linear Regresion with Claiam dataset

We use the insurance dataset stored in the project’s data/ folder. We first load the dataset.


```{r}
#| label: load_data

insurance <- read_csv("../data/insuranceKaggle.csv")

glimpse(insurance)
```


## Insurance Charges vs. Age


```{r}
#| label: plot charge vs age

ggplot(insurance, aes(x = age, y = charges)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 16) + 
  labs(
    title = "Insurance Charges by Age",
    x = "Age",
    y = "Charges"
  )

```



## Smoker and Charges

```{r}
#| label: plot charge vs smoker

ggplot(insurance, aes(x = smoker, y = charges)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_bw(base_size = 16) +
  labs(
    title = "Insurance Charges by Smoking Status",
    x = "Smoker",
    y = "Charges"
  )
```




For a simple regression, base R can fit the model directly:

```{r}
#| label: lm fit

lm_model <- lm(charges ~ age, data = insurance)

summary(lm_model)

```

From the model fitting, the simple regression line is given by 

$$ \hat{\text{charge}} = `r lm_model$coefficients[1]` + `r lm_model$coefficients[2]` \text{age}. $$

Generate the prediction and add it to the data frame

```{r}
insurance$prediction <- predict(lm_model, insurance)
```



## Residual Plots


```{r}
insurance$residual <- residuals(lm_model)
```


Plot the standard residuals vs fitted plot (diagnostic plot)

```{r}
insurance %>% ggplot(aes(x=prediction , y=  residual)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Residual vs. Fitted Values",
    x = "Fitted values",
    y = "Residuals (errors)"
  )
```
